Key Finding: Evidence-informed AI governance: Multi-Criteria Analysis, Regulatory Sandboxes, harmonisation. Europe's leadership in international AI regulation.
LDA topic modelling of 78 Chinese AI policies: 7 themes including pilot zone construction, social governance, infrastructure. Growing central-local coordination.
Journal/Source: Proceedings of the Association for Information Science and Technology 62(1)

Key Finding: Multiple Streams Framework: problems, policies, politics must converge for AI agenda change. Policy entrepreneurs key to adoption in Mexican state public sector.
AI infrastructure and research capacity predict national competitiveness. USA leads via public-private partnerships; Singapore via Model AI Governance Framework.
Urban AI megaproject in healthcare: enhances efficiency and patient care; challenges include data privacy, ethics, infrastructure. Policy recommendations for smart healthcare governance.
Global AI indices create path dependence on policy; AI framed as competitiveness not ethics, limiting policy alternatives including AI ethics.
Discourse network analysis of 6,421 statements: German actors frame AI as technology/innovation policy, not civil rights. National government struggles to steer AI agenda.

City/Context: Argentina; Brazil; Chile; Colombia; Mexico; Uruguay
Key Finding: AI policy design in Latin America: political regimes and governance modes shape different design spaces for national AI strategies across 6 countries.
AIdeology: AI is not only technology but ideology shaping urban spaces, governance, sustainability narratives. Critical theory linking AI to spatial inequality.
Five governance modes for urban sustainability: participatory, collaborative, multilevel, smart (AI/IoT), network. Smart governance prominent since 2015.
GenAI city brains reshape anticipatory urban governance and public policy. 14 semi-structured interviews 2022-23. Policy mobility to Malaysia and Saudi Arabia.
AI governance in BRICS nations: ethical embedding, strong legal frameworks, balance of innovation/accountability. Inclusive participatory governance recommended.
SLR: ICTs change street-level discretion via removing face-to-face interaction, standardising processes, enhancing monitoring. Bureaucrats resist ICT standardisation.
Participatory governance as mechanism for inclusive AI contributing to social good. Policy recommendations at national and global levels.
Government chatbots in public encounters: three puzzles — discretion, emotion, accountability. Raises democratic accountability questions.
Oxford AI Readiness Index: AI advancement insufficient alone — privacy, transparency, inclusion, accountability principles key. Advanced democracies often ready but not responsible.
Replication study in China: algorithmic explainability enhances public trust across cultural contexts. Stronger effects in high-discretion situations.
Vertical rule coherence not wealth determines AI public value yield. UAE pilots become hundreds of services; Kuwait stays in pilot mode despite equal fiscal resources.
AI in Canadian public service: applied to administration, bilingual services, policy analysis, adjudication, compliance monitoring.
Survey experiment (n=4,200): public prefers local over national AI in policing. Institutional context matters more than technical features.
Street-level bureaucrats intend to use GPTs even when prohibited when private-sector competitors have AI access. Mixed methods: focus groups (n=14) survey (n=279). Promethean moment of GenAI.
Conceptual framework for AI in public administration: accountability requires explainability, interpretability, transparency. AI systems largely under private IP raising accountability challenges.
Five-layer smart bureaucracy model for Indonesia's new capital: strategic, interagency, operations, monitoring, digital infrastructure. Comparative with Putrajaya and Naypyidaw.
Effectiveness-efficiency paradox in AI public services (n=805 employees; n=699 citizens). Human-AI collaboration moderates the paradox.
Accountable discretion concept. Boston DoIT AI sandboxes. GenAI redistributes discretion across institutional levels. Harvard Kennedy School.
Smart city AI and digital twin convergence: metaverse, privacy-preserving AI, edge AI reshaping smart city management. Large-scale datasets to actionable intelligence remains managerial challenge.
Smartness narratives in eldercare: governments, corporations, investors diverge. Alibaba CityBrain in Hangzhou exemplifies real-time data exploitation for anticipatory governance.
Journal/Source: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers 50(3)

Key Finding: AI-enabled governance in TCM enterprise clusters: lifecycle model across adaptation, maturity, decline stages. Reduces costs, improves efficiency, fosters stakeholder collaboration (SDG 8 & 9).
Dubai smart city governance: e-government, clean transport. AI and big data for smart urban management. Lessons for Los Angeles, Santiago and coastal cities globally.
AI governance frameworks by tech conglomerates, policymakers, IGOs. Key CSR dimensions: accountability, transparency, fairness, privacy, safety, cybersecurity.
SLR 309 AI ethics articles: design concerns (bias & data) vs human-AI interaction concerns (privacy & surveillance). EU Trustworthy AI Guidelines alignment with company law.
Smart city control rooms rewire local governance in India: extend central government control, legitimise ICT companies as urban development actors.
Journal/Source: International Journal of Urban and Regional Research

Key Finding: Nested Complexity framework: AI introduces technological, ethical, and regulatory challenges within urban/organisational complexity. Adaptive iterative leadership required.

City/Context: 10 countries inc. China; UAE; S. Africa
Key Finding: Econometric analysis 2000-2022: AI increases CO2 but governance effectiveness and environmental sustainability reduce it. Policy must integrate AI governance with climate action (SDG 7, 9, 13, 16).
Hofstede cultural dimensions impact AI-ESG application. Positive organisational attitudes increase AI-ESG effects; formal policies alone are too rigid. Cultural sensitivity essential.
Smart grid AI reduces peak electricity demand by 25%. 2024: microgrid-level controls scaled. Public-private AI governance of urban energy infrastructure.
ESG integral to fintech: AI-driven ESG scoring systems and blockchain supply-chain tracking enhance sustainability investment accountability and governance.
AI Integration Strategy (Sept 2024): 7-principle strategic framework. Cross-departmental governance committee across 50+ municipal services. Fail fast pilot approach.
City AI strategic framework: technology systems + application scenarios + educational literacy + governance schemes. AI as complete industry and governance object.
Rise of AI Urbanism: strategic shift from smart city to AI urbanism. AI as urban stakeholder. Strategic governance challenges around autonomy, equity, housing.
AI Localism in Practice: cities govern AI through procurement standards, public registers, participatory strategy. Foundational strategic framing for city-level AI governance.
Three research directions: (1) what is urban AI, (2) AI-city interdependencies, (3) governance challenges and opportunities. Strategic research agenda for urban AI.
AI Register; MaaS governance; climate footprint calculator 2024; AI housing chatbot 2025. Equity gaps among older/rural populations identified.
Algorithm register; citizen-led AI ethics panels; digital sovereignty principles. Participatory model contrasted with Singapore's centralised approach.
Algorithm register aligned with Cities Coalition for Digital Rights schema (2023). Model for differential privacy and algorithmic accountability.
Citation: South Florida Journal of Development (2025); CIDOB GOUAI
Journal/Source: South Florida Journal of Development / CIDOB

Key Finding: Digitale Menschenrechte (Digital Human Rights Charter): city-level rights framework; widely cited post-2022 as ethical governance model.
AI Action Plan 2023; Local Law 3 on biometric identifiers; law requiring companies to disclose hiring algorithms.
Responsible GenAI experimentation: piloted internal summarisation and resident-facing assistants with guardrails and problem-discovery iterative approach.
Model AI Governance Framework (PDPC); Virtual Singapore digital twin. Centralised governance: explainability, fairness, human involvement.
Citation: South Florida Journal of Development (2025); MDPI Smart Cities (2025)
Journal/Source: South Florida Journal of Development / Smart Cities

Key Finding: Expanded smart governance 2024: AI ethics panels, cross-cultural content testing for diverse expatriate population.
NLP/bibliometric: 4,021 governance+AI/smart city Scopus documents 2000-2022. Post-2022 surge. Six research clusters: governance, privacy, AI, smart city, participation, policy.

FinTech exerts strong positive impact on AI adoption at early/middle stages. Human capital shows nonlinear effect. Policy: foster FinTech ecosystems, digital education, renewable-powered AI infrastructure (SDG 7, 9, 13).
Bibliometric of 264 finance review papers: four clusters — corporate finance/markets, FinTech/AI innovations, social finance/inclusion, CSR/corporate governance.
Big data, AI, ML transformative symbiosis in FinTech. RegTech and AI ethics identified as key future challenges for financial technology governance.

RegTech enabling near real-time financial market regulation (MiFID II & MiFIR). Regulatory software shapes reporting standards. Critique: democratic deficit and accountability concerns. EU AI Act referenced.

Risk assessment and regulation algorithms for robo-advisory FinTech platforms in smart cities. ML-based platform risk prediction model; accuracy of 88%. Black box regulatory system for robo-advisory algorithms.

3.5-decade evolutionary review of AI in banking, financial services, insurance: RAI governance frameworks not yet incorporated by fintech or incumbent organisations. RAI critical for DeFi. Dominant AI areas: investments, securities, market making, lending, compliance.
SLR 157 articles: AI in banking — algorithmic trading, RegTech, customer service, explainability. Black-box AI raises regulatory concerns. Transparency imperative for compliance.

City/Context: European stock markets (Athens SE / MiFID II)
Key Finding: Algorithmic trading (AT) induces herding 14x more than non-AT under MiFID II. AT-herding increases with international volatility. Critical implications for stock market regulators.
Bank RegTech improves corporate investment efficiency by ~18% per SD increase. RegTech strengthens governance capabilities, mitigates operational risk, reduces financing constraints.

AI innovation reduces stock price crash risk (SPCR): strengthens internal governance, increases financial transparency, reduces bad-news hoarding by management. Corporate governance mechanisms mediate the effect.
AI enhances investment efficiency via complex system analysis and real-time decision making. Digital intelligence finance entering a new era.
Multi-task deep neural network for insider trading identification in securities market. Accuracy gains over traditional models. AI as regulatory tool for market fairness and order.

Smart ESG framework for DeFi: BART model (Blockchain Automated Regulatory Tool), Dynamic Predictive Regulatory framework, Incentive Dynamic Governance Index. Multi-level regulatory system for DeFi markets.
Journal/Source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management 32(6)

Key Finding: FinTech substitution hypothesis confirmed across 10,000+ financial institutions. Traditional banks in countries with stronger regulatory frameworks benefit more from FinTech expansion.
Journal/Source: Journal of International Financial Management & Accounting 37(1)

Key Finding: AI tokens are net transmitters of market shocks; energy sector is net receiver. Dynamic connectedness increased during COVID-19 and Russia-Ukraine war. Governance implications for AI asset regulation.

Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect liberalisation: information environment and corporate governance mechanisms mediate effects on debt maturity structure. AI/digital tools enhance foreign investor governance monitoring.
